title: Postoperative Prophylaxis of Cystic Echinococcosis with Albendazole and Praziquantel: A Retrospective Cohort Study
content: Background/Objectives: Cystic echinococcosis (hydatidosis) is a zoonotic parasitic disease primarily managed surgically, yet postoperative recurrences affect 2–22% of patients. Albendazole is standard for prophylaxis, but recurrences still occur. This study evaluated whether combining albendazole with praziquantel improves prevention of postoperative recurrences while assessing tolerability. Methods: This single-centre, retrospective, two-arm cohort study included 60 patients (aged 19–77, mean 43.9 ± 15.1 years) undergoing surgery for hepatic, pulmonary and/or abdominal hydatidosis between April 2024 and April 2026. All patients received albendazole (400 mg twice daily for 2–4 months). Thirty patients additionally received praziquantel (25 mg/kg/day for 10 days) in the first three postoperative months. Follow-up was systematically shorter in the combination arm (median 10 months, range 6–18) versus the albendazole-only arm (median 24 months, range 6–24). Results: Significant baseline imbalances existed between arms (14/15 covariates with |SMD| > 0.10), with the combination group having more abdominal and fertile cysts plus higher baseline transaminases. Of 118 resected cysts, two recurrences (6.7%) occurred in the albendazole arm at 12 months (incidence rate 3.73/100 person-years). No recurrences were observed in the combination arm within its shorter follow-up window. Adverse events were similar (43.3% vs 50.0%; adjusted OR 1.09, 95% CI 0.33–3.57), with no significant added hepatotoxicity after adjustment. Conclusions: Albendazole plus praziquantel was well tolerated. Due to baseline imbalances, differential follow-up, and limited events, these data do not support firm conclusions on superior efficacy. The hypothesis-generating signal warrants confirmation in a prospective, randomized trial with long-term balanced follow-up and optimized dosing.
